class.name: Mode7ScanlineOverride
class.brief_description: A resource that holds per-scanline transform data for Mode 7 perspective rendering.
class.description:
A [Resource] used by [Mode7Sprite2D] (and indirectly [Mode7TileMapLayer]) to store one entry in the per-scanline "scanline table" that drives Mode 7-style perspective/rotation effects.
Each instance encodes a single transform row: a 2x2 affine matrix (rotation + scale + skew), a translation offset, and a pivot point. The interpolation mode ([member interpolation]) determines how adjacent rows are blended in the shader.
The transforms are stored canonically as a [Transform2D], but you can also read/write decomposed rotation, scale, and skew properties for convenience.

members.member: The canonical 2x2 affine matrix (columns 0 and 1) plus translation (column 2). Decomposed properties ([member rotation], [member scale], [member skew]) all read through this.
Rotation in radians, decomposed from [member transform].
Scale factor (inverted internally), decomposed from [member transform]. Values below 0.1 are clamped to prevent division-by-zero artifacts.
Skew in radians, decomposed from [member transform].
The vanishing point (in normalized 0..1 texture UV space) around which the transform is applied. Defaults to center (0.5, 0.5).

How the shader blends this entry with its neighbors: - [constant Mode7ScanlineOverride.INTERPOLATION_NONE]: Nearest-neighbor snap (each row uses exactly one entry's transform). - [constant Mode7ScanlineOverride.INTERPOLATION_LERP]: Linear interpolation between adjacent entries. - [constant Mode7ScanlineOverride.INTERPOLATION_PROJECTION]: Perspective projection via inverse-depth interpolation, using entry[0] as top/horizon and the last entry as bottom/close anchor.

constants.constant: Nearest-neighbor: snap to this entry's transform for its UV band. No blending between rows.
Linear interpolation between adjacent entries in the override array.
Perspective projection via per-scanline inverse-depth interpolation. Uses entry[0] as top/horizon and entry[last] as bottom/close anchor.
